title: Platelet-Derived Vesicles Drive Macrophage Pyroptosis in Dabie Bandavirus Infection
excerpt: Platelet-derived extracellular vesicles induced by Dabie bandavirus trigger macrophage pyroptosis and amplify inflammatory responses, linking thrombocytopenia to severe disease outcomes.

content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Thursday, November 26, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Platelet-Derived Vesicles Drive Macrophage Pyroptosis in Dabie Bandavirus Infection by November 24, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 Platelet-Derived Vesicles Drive Macrophage Pyroptosis in Dabie Bandavirus Infection Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Extracellular vesicles released by platelets during Dabie bandavirus infection directly trigger macrophage pyroptosis and amplify inflammatory responses, according to findings published in PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases. Dabie bandavirus causes severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, an emerging tick-borne infectious disease characterized by remarkably increased morbidity and mortality across East Asia. In clinical settings, thrombocytopenia represents a hallmark pathogenic event and an established independent predictor of multi-organ failure and poor clinical outcomes. Although Dabie bandavirus is known to bind to and replicate within host platelets, the precise contribution of activated platelets to disease pathogenesis has remained elusive. The researchers identified platelet-derived extracellular vesicles induced by Dabie bandavirus, designated DPEVs, as critical mediators of immune dysregulation. Upon viral activation, platelets release abundant vesicles that markedly heighten virus-driven inflammation while driving recipient macrophages into a distinct pro-inflammatory and pyroptosis-prone state. When compared directly with extracellular vesicles generated through physical disruption, DPEVs displayed significantly enhanced immunostimulatory capacity. Mechanistically, the study showed that DPEVs compromise mitochondrial integrity and stimulate the production of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species inside macrophages, thereby triggering the downstream pyroptotic death program. This sequence defines a previously unrecognized pathogenic axis linking viral platelet activation, extracellular vesicle signaling, mitochondrial injury, and macrophagic pyroptosis during Dabie bandavirus infection. Beyond promoting inflammatory damage, DPEVs incorporated viral components, suggesting a potential dual role in mediating both inflammatory amplification and viral dissemination. By establishing a direct mechanistic link between thrombocytopenia and clinical severity in severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, the findings position these virus-induced extracellular vesicles as key amplifiers of inflammation with notable potential value as clinical biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
